summary.headline: Sai Parenterals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9% QoQ to INR196.1 crore, with gross margin up to 47.5% and EBITDA margin to 21.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations rose 9% sequentially to INR196.1 crore, with H1 FY27 revenue of INR376 crore against a full-year target of INR750 crore. Gross margin improved from 40.9% to 47.5% as raw material cost fell about 3% on tighter inventory controls, lifting EBITDA 67% QoQ to INR41.4 crore (21.1% margin). Depreciation rose to INR25.1 crore from INR8.1 crore on Noumed and Sai Prathyak asset capitalisation, but PAT still grew 33% QoQ to INR10.5 crore. Management reclassified other income below EBITDA, restating Q1 EBITDA to INR24.7 crore (13.7%). Acquisitions of 60% in Saicriti Pharma and Sai Prathyak Laboratories closed, and the Adelaide and Unit III projects are moving towards operation.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin to be kept above 45% in coming quarters, per management.
EBITDA margin expected to comfortably exceed the approximately 17% full-year guidance.
FY27 revenue expected to comfortably cross the INR750 crore target; H2 seasonally stronger.
Unit III capacity ramps from Q4 FY27, with most incremental volume to Australia and New Zealand.

Adelaide facility commissioning expected January 2027 (slightly behind earlier plan due to Iran-conflict logistics); TGA inspection expected Q2 2027; commercial supply after licence. Inventory at Noumed to fall from 9-10 months towards 5-6 months.
Sai Prathyak to start external R&D/CRO contracts from Q4 FY27, with revenue from FY28. FY28 guidance promised on the next earnings call (Jan/Feb 2027).
Debt expected to peak in FY26 per management wording and decline from FY28 and FY29; Saicriti project debt drawn at subsidiary level as construction progresses.
capex_capacity: Unit III Bhongir expansion almost complete; new block to start commencing December 2026. Capacity to rise from 85.5 million to 155 million units a month (+81%). Adds high-capacity ointment, high-speed capsule filling and liquid oral lines.

Saicriti Pharma new injectable facility at Gummadidala, targeted completion July 2027. Four process lines ordered (liquid and lyophilised, GLP pre-filled syringe, combi-filling, dry powder, ampoule). Total project cost INR215 crore; Sai contribution INR83.83 crore for 60%; promoters fund 40% of equity; project debt with 3-year moratorium and 7-year repayment. Injectable capacity to reach about 154.66 million units. Jeedimetla Units I and II to be discontinued after commissioning.
Adelaide (Noumed) facility: AUD46 million invested of AUD53 million planned; AUD20 million Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant supports the program.
H1 FY27 capex about INR70 crore, mainly Adelaide and Unit III. Total borrowing INR357 crore at 30 September 2026 vs about INR320 crore in March 2026; cash and equivalents INR129 crore.
Sai Prathyak has 36-molecule annual development capacity and 174 molecules and 285 SKUs in portfolio; 98 in-house dossiers, 45 commercialised and 76 under development targeted for FY28.
demand_pricing: Noumed renewed a 7.5-year exclusive OTC supply contract with EBOS Group (TerryWhite and Pharmacy Choice brands) from 1 July 2026, valued AUD202 million.

Wesfarmers (Priceline and Pharmacy Health) OTC contract renewed on 25 August 2026 for 3 years at AUD30 million (about INR204 crore). Combined contracted Australia OTC book: AUD232 million (about INR1,506 crore).

Philippines: 11 molecules and 22 SKUs added in Q2, mainly cardiovascular. Management said these fall under the existing USD14 million regular contract; the USD11 million anti-TB contract commercials start after January 2027.

Management targets Southeast Asia, Latin America and Middle East for injectables over the next two to three years; no US FDA launch planned for at least two to three years unless a CMO client brings a product.
Management plans to announce oncology mAbs and biosimilars plans (global focus) in about a month, subject to board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Heet (Axis Capital): Any quantitative guidance on sales growth or margins after the strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin was the key driver and will be kept above 45%. Unit III output from Q4 and Sai Prathyak revenue from Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28 should take revenue comfortably past INR750 crore and EBITDA margin above 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao (Plutus Wealth): Why did receivables rise to about INR250 crore in H1, and what is the ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export and CDMO receivables age under 120 days, and domestic branded generics 120-150 days. The Q2 build reflected lower collections from two large export customers and sales bunched in the last 1-1.5 months. Domestic ageing to be below 120 days within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao: Is the 11-molecule Philippines addition part of the USD11 million contract, and what is Sai Prathyak's revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The 11 molecules were added to the regular USD14 million contract; the USD11 million is a separate anti-TB contract. For Sai Prathyak, management has not yet modelled numbers and promised guidance on the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Murali (individual investor): Will the company pursue US FDA for injectables, and what is the multi-year growth CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: No US FDA launch for at least two to three years; US FDA is an option only for CMO client products. FY28 guidance to come on the next call; no three-year CAGR given.

qa_highlights.question: Gopal Bhatt (Baroda BNP Paribas AM): Why was H1 FY27 operating cash flow negative, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR113.1 crore outflow in other financial liabilities for the IPO-linked OFS and about INR49 crore decline in trade payables and current liabilities. Management said H1 FY26 is not comparable because it was standalone only. The call did not reconcile the INR201 crore operating cash outflow figure that the analyst quoted to management's cash flow figures.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavika Singhvi (Niveshaay): How are CDMO partners and products selected, and what are the key challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the three-year plan is backward and forward integration across all dosage forms, with in-house development via Sai Prathyak. Challenges were integration of subsidiaries and capex execution; management is adding senior KMP and expects a further substantial increase in the next three to four months.

risks_watch: Receivables build (about INR250 crore in H1) and domestic ageing of 120-150 days; watch normalisation in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Adelaide commissioning slipped to January 2027, with TGA inspection expected Q2 2027; logistics disruption linked to the Iran conflict.

Operating cash flow was negative in H1 FY27 per the analyst's reading of the cash flow statement; management's explanation relied on OFS outflow and payables decline and was not fully reconciled on the call.
Debt rising to INR357 crore with further project capex; Saicriti project debt to be drawn as construction progresses; FY28 deleveraging is management's stated expectation.
Management bandwidth and integration across four subsidiaries; KMP additions expected in the next three to four months.
Pending items to watch: Sai Prathyak FY28 guidance, oncology mAbs and biosimilars plan, the Jeedimetla site decision, and the balance 40% of Sai Prathyak (right of first refusal).
Gross margin sustainability above 45% depends on inventory controls; management said this is just the beginning of the inventory work.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 delivery and margin trajectory, but evasive on quantified guidance: FY28 numbers, Sai Prathyak revenue, and the mAbs/biosimilars plan were all deferred to later disclosures. Management was defensive on the operating cash flow and receivables questions, and the CFO's absence left the financial detail to the Chairman.
key_quotes: Gross margin rose from 40.9% in Q1 to 47.5% in Q2. Raw material cost actually fell by about 3% even as revenue grew by 9%.
We will be investing INR98.8 crores of IPO proceeds, that is INR83.83 crores in Saicriti Pharma, and I already invested INR15 crores in Prathyak Laboratories, each for a 60% stake.

As of now we have not worked on the numbers, Amol, but by next quarter earnings call I should be able to give some guided guidance on this Sai Prathyak side because we keep on working with so many clients.

But as we are already doing this, we also want to extend our services for the outside people, which will be a revenue model for us, and it will be an added revenue to the -- because we have 36 products capacity at Prathyak as of today.
